article_content: 'Transitioning back to civilian life after military service can be difficult for many veterans.  However, an innovative program at Syracuse University's Whitman School of Management is working to ease this transition through entrepreneurship. The Entrepreneurship Bootcamp for Veterans with Disabilities (EBV) equips U.S. war veterans with essential business skills, empowering them to create thriving businesses. Developed by Air Force veteran and Syracuse University professor Mike Haynie, the EBV addresses the unique employment challenges faced by disabled veterans.  John Raftery, a former Marine who struggled with post-traumatic stress disorder and unstable employment after his service, is a testament to the program's success. After attending the EBV in 2007, Raftery founded Patriot Contractors, Inc., a now flourishing Dallas-based business.  He recently returned to Syracuse to receive the EBV's Veteran Entrepreneur of the Year award.  The program, funded entirely by donations, is available to veterans with service-connected disabilities.  Another veteran, Joshua Pitcher, who sustained serious injuries in Iraq, is utilizing the EBV to develop his furniture-making business. The program involves online learning, an intensive nine-day bootcamp, and ongoing mentorship. Since its inception at Syracuse in 2007, the EBV has expanded to other universities, forming the EBV Consortium of Schools.  The consortium includes UCLA Anderson, Florida State University, Texas A&M University, and Purdue University.  Elaine Hagan, executive director of the Harold Price Center for Entrepreneurial Studies at UCLA Anderson, noted the veterans' valuable leadership and teamwork skills. The EBV emphasizes not only practical business skills but also inspires veterans by connecting them with prominent figures, reinforcing their potential for success.'

article_content: The Titanic, famously known for its tragic maiden voyage, is seen in a new light thanks to a unique project. Russian photo editor Anton Logvynenko has colorized original black and white images, breathing new life into the iconic ship's story. Logvynenko painstakingly colorized photographs, showcasing the Titanic from its construction in Belfast to its fully furnished decks. He even colorized images of well-wishers bidding farewell. Using current technology, Logvynenko gave authentic color to the original images. Launched to commemorate the 100th anniversary of the sinking, the project gained popularity after being shared on blogs. The RMS Titanic, one of the most opulent liners ever built and the largest steamship of its time, struck an iceberg on its maiden voyage from Southampton to New York City, sinking on April 15, 1912, resulting in 1,517 deaths. Logvynenko's project showcases the ship's luxurious interior, reminiscent of hotels like The Ritz, with ornate ceilings and plush carpets. First-class cabins mirrored the finest hotel rooms, and Logvynenko's work highlights the sumptuous bedding, carpets, and artistic decorations. The colorized photos reveal details like the ornate ceilings and ivy in the Cafe Parisien, which was designed to resemble a Parisian sidewalk cafe. The project also features images of passengers enjoying amenities like the gymnasium, a library, a swimming pool, a squash court, a Turkish bath, and an electric bath. The scale of the ship's construction is also evident, from its time in the gantry at Belfast to its departure from Southampton. Logvynenko's colorized images capture the Titanic's majesty before its tragic end. For more, visit his website, Titanic In Color.

article_content: '(CNN) -- Russell Westbrook scored an impressive 43 points, but it wasn't enough to prevent the Oklahoma City Thunder from losing Game 4 of the NBA Finals to the Miami Heat, 104-98.  This marks the Thunder's third consecutive loss in the series.  Trailing 2-1 going into the game, the Thunder started strong, building a 17-point lead in the first quarter. However, the Heat rallied, narrowing the gap to three points by halftime, largely due to LeBron James's influence. James finished with 26 points and 12 assists but sat out the final minutes with a quadriceps cramp.  His crucial three-pointer, however, put Miami ahead 97-94 before he left the court.  'The ball was swung to me... I just wanted to step up and make a play with the limited mobility that I had,' James said after the game, according to NBA.com.  'My teammates were able to close it from there.'  Heat point guard Mario Chalmers also had a key performance, scoring 25 points in 34 minutes. Chalmers, relatively quiet in the previous games (only two points in Game 3), made the most of his opportunities. 'I think they kind of forgot about me and let me roam a little bit more tonight,' Chalmers said, referencing his open shots. Chalmers has a history of strong performances in crucial games. 'He's done it time and time again in big games in college, big games in the pros,' Heat coach Erik Spoelstra commented.  'You can't teach that. He gave us a lift tonight that we really needed.' The game's final minutes were marked by errors from Oklahoma City.  With less than 20 seconds left, Westbrook fouled Chalmers with five seconds still on the shot clock. 'It was just a miscommunication on my part,' Westbrook admitted. 'Nothing I can do about it now.'  When asked about media criticism from the off-season, Westbrook stated,  'What you guys say doesn't make me happy or make me sad. It's not me against the world. It's me and my teammates trying to win.' Game 5 is scheduled for Thursday in Miami.'

article_content: 'New research raises concerns about the safety of tackle football for children under 12. A study published in 'Neurology' examined cognitive function in 42 former NFL players, finding that early exposure to tackle football (before age 12) was linked to increased cognitive difficulties later in life, such as problems with memory, thinking, and mental agility. This association persisted even after accounting for the total number of years played and concussions sustained. Interestingly, both groups, those with early tackle football experience and those without, performed below average on cognitive assessments.  The research team, led by Julie Stam and Robert Stern, highlighted the potential vulnerability of developing brains to repetitive head impacts. While acknowledging the benefits of youth sports, they emphasized the need for greater safety measures, potentially reconsidering tackle football for young children. Christopher Filley, in an editorial accompanying the study, stressed the urgency of understanding these effects, especially considering the millions of children participating in youth football and the high incidence of head impacts in this sport.'

En studie publicerad i 'Neurology' undersökte kognitiv funktion hos 42 före detta NFL-spelare och fann att tidig exponering för amerikansk fotboll (före 12 års ålder) var kopplad till ökade kognitiva svårigheter senare i livet, såsom problem med minne, tänkande och mental smidighet. Denna koppling kvarstod även efter att man tagit hänsyn till det totala antalet år som spelats och hjärnskakningar som uppstått. Intressant nog presterade båda grupperna, de med tidig erfarenhet av amerikansk fotboll och de utan, under genomsnittet på kognitiva bedömningar. Forskargruppen, ledd av Julie Stam och Robert Stern, betonade den potentiella sårbarheten hos hjärnor under utveckling för upprepade huvudtrauma. Samtidigt som de erkände fördelarna med ungdomsidrott, betonade de behovet av större säkerhetsåtgärder och att potentiellt ompröva amerikansk fotboll för små barn. article_content: 'To demonstrate the effectiveness of its advertising, Facebook has teamed up with data company Datalogix. This partnership allows them to analyze whether users who view ads on the platform subsequently purchase those products in physical stores. Datalogix accesses anonymized purchasing information from around 70 million American households via loyalty programs at over 1,000 retailers. By comparing this data with anonymized Facebook user information, they can ascertain if an ad view led to a purchase. Early results from 45 campaigns indicate a \$3 return for every \$1 spent on Facebook ads. However, privacy advocates are worried about user consent and data transparency, particularly because users can't opt out directly through Facebook. Instead, they have to navigate to Datalogix's website, accessible via a link in Facebook's help center.  While Facebook claims individual user data isn't shared with advertisers, and they are using an external auditor to ensure data privacy, the practice is still under scrutiny.'
translated_content: 'För att visa effektiviteten i sin annonsering har Facebook samarbetat med dataföretaget Datalogix. Detta partnerskap gör det möjligt för dem att analysera om användare som ser annonser på plattformen därefter köper dessa produkter i fysiska butiker. Datalogix har tillgång till anonymiserad köpinformation från cirka 70 miljoner amerikanska hushåll via lojalitetsprogram hos över 1 000 återförsäljare. Genom att jämföra dessa data med anonymiserad Facebook-användarinformation kan de fastställa om en annonsvisning ledde till ett köp. Tidiga resultat från 45 kampanjer tyder på 3 dollar i avkastning för varje dollar som spenderas på Facebook-annonser. Integritetsförespråkare är dock oroliga över användarnas samtycke och datatransparens, särskilt eftersom användare inte kan välja bort direkt via Facebook. Istället måste de navigera till Datalogixs webbplats, tillgänglig via en länk i Facebooks hjälpcenter. Även om Facebook hävdar att individuell användardata inte delas med annonsörer, och de använder en extern revisor för att säkerställa datasekretess, granskas praxisen fortfarande.'

article_content: Despite research indicating that wearing makeup during workouts can hinder calorie burning, a significant portion of British women choose to wear it at the gym.  This preference was highlighted by celebrity examples: opera singer Katherine Jenkins wore light makeup during the London Marathon, while TV personality Fern Britton opted for a bare-faced look after her spin class. A survey commissioned by online beauty retailer Escentual.com revealed that approximately two-thirds of women admit to using cosmetics while exercising.  55% prefer light makeup, while an additional 11% opt for a full face.  This trend extends to public events, with 20% wearing full makeup for marathons or fun runs, and over half choosing at least light makeup. Even for a casual jog, 44% stated they would apply some beauty products.  Beauty expert Emma Leslie suggests this reflects the social aspect of gyms and a desire to maintain a polished appearance.  The increasing availability of workout-proof makeup further facilitates this trend.  The survey also revealed widespread makeup use in other public settings:  most women wear full makeup for shopping trips, while over half of mothers do so for the school run.  Job interviews, unsurprisingly, see the highest makeup usage, with 99% of women choosing to wear some.

Detta illustreras av kändisar: operasångerskan Katherine Jenkins bar lätt smink under London Marathon, medan TV-personligheten Fern Britton valde en osminkad look efter sin spinningklass. En undersökning beställd av online-skönhetsåterförsäljaren Escentual.com visade att ungefär två tredjedelar av kvinnorna erkänner att de använder kosmetika under träning. 55 % föredrar lätt smink, medan ytterligare 11 % väljer en fullständig makeup. Denna trend sträcker sig till offentliga evenemang, där 20 % bär fullständig makeup för maraton eller löptävlingar, och över hälften väljer åtminstone lätt smink. Även för en avslappnad joggingtur uppgav 44 % att de skulle applicera vissa skönhetsprodukter. Skönhetsexperten Emma Leslie föreslår att detta speglar den sociala aspekten av gym och en önskan att bibehålla ett polerat utseende. Den ökande tillgängligheten av träningssäkert smink underlättar ytterligare denna trend. Undersökningen avslöjade också en utbredd användning av smink i andra offentliga miljöer: de flesta kvinnor bär fullständig makeup för shoppingturer, medan över hälften av mammorna gör det för skolhämtningen. Anställningsintervjuer, föga förvånande, visar den högsta sminkanvändningen, där 99 % av kvinnorna väljer att använda någon form av smink.
